title: 144. Quantitative Relationships & Measurement: Proportionality from Data Tables
description: A comprehensive mathematics curriculum progressing from foundational numeracy and core mathematical concepts to algebra, geometry, calculus, linear algebra, probability, statistics, discrete mathematics, optimization, mathematical foundations of AI, advanced pure mathematics, and emerging research methods.

questions.concept: Identifying Direct Proportionality from a Data Table
questions.learningObjective: Determine whether a data table represents a directly proportional relationship.
questions.question:
The table shows values of \(x\) and \(y\).
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}x&2&5&8\\\hline y&8&20&32\end{array}
\]
Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The values are not proportional because both quantities increase.

options.label: B
options.text: The values are directly proportional with constant \(4\).

questions.explanation: The ratios are \(\frac{8}{2}=\frac{20}{5}=\frac{32}{8}=4\), so \(y=4x\). Both quantities increasing does not disprove proportionality; the constant ratio confirms it.
questions.hint: Check ratios using complete nonzero table columns.

questions.concept: Finding a Missing Value in a Proportional Table
questions.learningObjective: Determine a missing value in a directly proportional data table.
questions.question:
The table below shows a proportional relationship between \(x\) and \(y\).
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
x & 3 & 5 & 8\\
\hline
y & 12 & 20 & ?
\end{array}
\]
What is the missing value of \(y\)?
questions.explanation:
The constant of proportionality is \(\frac{12}{3}=4\). Therefore, when \(x=8\),
\[
y=4\times 8=32
\]
The missing value is \(32\). Option B is incorrect because \(8\times 3=24\), which uses the wrong constant.
questions.hint: Find the constant of proportionality from a complete column, then apply it to the given \(x\)-value.

questions.concept: Equation of a Directly Proportional Relationship from a Table
questions.learningObjective: Identify the equation representing a proportional relationship shown in a table.
questions.question:
The table below shows values of \(x\) and \(y\).
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
x & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4\\
\hline
y & 5 & 10 & 15 & 20
\end{array}
\]
Which equation represents the relationship?
questions.explanation: For each pair, \(\frac{y}{x}=5\). Thus the relationship is multiplicative: \(y=5x\). Option B is additive and would give \(y=6\), \(7\), \(8\), \(9\), which does not match the table.
questions.hint: Find the unit rate before extending a proportional table.

questions.concept: Recognizing Non-Proportional Data in a Table
questions.learningObjective: Identify why a data table does not represent direct proportionality.
questions.question:
The table below shows values of \(x\) and \(y\).
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
x & 2 & 4 & 6\\
\hline
y & 5 & 9 & 13
\end{array}
\]
Which statement is correct?

options.label: A
options.text: The relationship is not proportional, because \(\frac{y}{x}\) is not constant.

options.label: B
options.text: The relationship is proportional, because \(y\) increases by \(4\) each time \(x\) increases by \(2\).

questions.explanation:
Check the ratios:
\[
\frac{5}{2}=2.5,\qquad \frac{9}{4}=2.25,\qquad \frac{13}{6}\approx 2.17
\]
The ratios are not equal, so the relationship is not proportional. Option B describes an additive pattern, not a proportional one.
questions.hint: Check ratios using complete nonzero table columns.

questions.learningObjective: Determine a missing value using the constant of proportionality.
questions.question:
The table below represents a proportional relationship.
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
x & 2 & 3 & 4\\
\hline
y & 8 & 12 & ?
\end{array}
\]
What is the missing value of \(y\)?
questions.explanation: The constant ratio is \(\frac{8}{2}=\frac{12}{3}=4\), so the missing value is \(4\times 4=16\). The alternative \(15\) adds \(3\) to \(12\), but a unit increase in \(x\) increases \(y\) by \(4\), not \(3\).
questions.hint: Use a complete column to find the ratio \(\frac{y}{x}\), then apply it to the last \(x\)-value.

questions.learningObjective: Select the data table that represents a directly proportional relationship.
questions.question: Which table represents a directly proportional relationship?
questions.explanation: In Table B, \(\frac{6}{1}=6\), \(\frac{12}{2}=6\), and \(\frac{18}{3}=6\), so the ratio is constant. In Table A, \(\frac{2}{1}=2\), \(\frac{5}{2}=2.5\), and \(\frac{8}{3}\approx 2.67\), so it is not proportional. Therefore, Table B represents direct proportionality.
questions.hint: Find the unit rate before extending a proportional table.

questions.learningObjective: Determine the constant of proportionality from a table that includes zero.
questions.question:
The table below shows a proportional relationship.
\[
\begin{array}{c|cccc}
x & 0 & 2 & 4 & 6\\
\hline
y & 0 & 6 & 12 & 18
\end{array}
\]
What is the constant of proportionality?
questions.explanation: Use any nonzero pair, for example \(\frac{6}{2}=3\). Also \(\frac{12}{4}=3\) and \(\frac{18}{6}=3\). The point \((0,0)\) is consistent with a proportional relationship. Therefore, the constant is \(3\). Option B is incorrect because \(6\) is the \(y\)-value when \(x=2\), not the ratio.
questions.hint: Check ratios using complete nonzero table columns.

questions.concept: Equation from a Proportional Data Table with Decimals
questions.learningObjective: Identify the equation for a proportional relationship from a table with decimal values.
questions.question:
The table below shows a proportional relationship.
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
x & 2 & 5 & 8\\
\hline
y & 3 & 7.5 & 12
\end{array}
\]
Which equation represents the relationship?
questions.explanation:
Using the pair \((5,7.5)\),
\[
k=\frac{7.5}{5}=1.5
\]
Check: \(2\times 1.5=3\) and \(8\times 1.5=12\), so the equation is \(y=1.5x\). Option A gives \(5\times 1.2=6\), which does not match the table.
questions.hint: Divide \(y\) by \(x\) for one column and check that the other columns give the same ratio.

questions.concept: Predicting a Value from a Proportional Table
questions.learningObjective: Use a proportional relationship from a table to predict a future value.
questions.question:
The table below shows a proportional relationship.
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
x & 3 & 6 & 9\\
\hline
y & 4 & 8 & 12
\end{array}
\]
If the pattern continues, what is \(y\) when \(x=12\)?
questions.explanation:
The table has a constant ratio.
\[
\begin{aligned}
k&=\frac{4}{3}=\frac{8}{6}=\frac{12}{9}\\
y\big|_{x=12}&=\frac{4}{3}\times 12=16
\end{aligned}
\]
The alternative \(15\) extends the last value by the increase in \(x\), \(12+(12-9)=15\), rather than preserving the ratio.
questions.hint: Find the unit rate before extending a proportional table.

questions.concept: Comparing Unit Rates from Proportional Tables
questions.learningObjective: Compare two proportional relationships by determining which has the greater unit rate.
questions.question:
The tables below show the output of two machines over time.
Machine A:
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Time (h)} & 2 & 4 & 6\\
\hline
\text{Output (units)} & 18 & 36 & 54
\end{array}
\]
Machine B:
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Time (h)} & 3 & 5 & 7\\
\hline
\text{Output (units)} & 24 & 40 & 56
\end{array}
\]
Which machine has the greater unit rate?
questions.explanation:
For Machine A, the unit rate is
\[
\frac{18}{2}=9\text{ units/h}
\]
For Machine B, the unit rate is
\[
\frac{24}{3}=8\text{ units/h}
\]
Since \(9>8\), Machine A has the greater unit rate. Option B is incorrect because Machine B produces \(8\text{ units}\) per hour, which is less than Machine A's \(9\text{ units}\) per hour.
questions.hint: Compare the output produced per hour by each machine.
